Attempt #1 03:00:00

Equation & Reference Sheet

Henderson–Hasselbalch
(weak acid)		$$\text{pH} = \text{pKa} + \log\frac{[A^-]}{[HA]}$$
Henderson–Hasselbalch
(weak base)		$$\text{pH} = \text{pKa} + \log\frac{[B]}{[BH^+]}$$
% IonizationWeak acid: $\text{pH} > \text{pKa}$ → more ionized. Weak base: $\text{pH} < \text{pKa}$ → more ionized.
Dilution$$C_1V_1 = C_2V_2$$
Alligation$$\text{Parts high} = |\text{low} - \text{desired}|$$$$\text{Parts low} = |\text{high} - \text{desired}|$$
% w/v$$\frac{\text{g solute}}{\text{100 mL solution}}\times 100\%$$
% w/w$$\frac{\text{g solute}}{\text{100 g preparation}}\times 100\%$$
% v/v$$\frac{\text{mL solute}}{\text{100 mL solution}}\times 100\%$$
Milliequivalents$$\text{mEq} = \frac{\text{mg}\times\text{valence}}{\text{MW}}$$
Milliosmoles$$\text{mOsmol} = \frac{\text{g}}{\text{MW}}\times n\times 1000$$
Tonicity (Sprowls)Uses $\Delta T_f$ (1% freezing-point depression) values to determine NaCl equivalence for isotonicity.
°F ↔ °C$$\text{°F} = \frac{9}{5}\text{°C} + 32$$$$\text{°C} = \frac{5}{9}(\text{°F} - 32)$$
Body Surface Area
(Mosteller)		$$\text{BSA }(m^2) = \sqrt{\frac{\text{height(cm)}\times\text{weight(kg)}}{3600}}$$
Creatinine Clearance
(Cockcroft-Gault)		$$\text{CrCl} = \frac{(140-\text{age})\times\text{wt(kg)}}{72\times S_{\text{Cr}}}\times 0.85\text{ if female}$$
Common conversions$1\text{ tsp} = 5\text{ mL}$, $1\text{ tbsp} = 15\text{ mL}$, $1\text{ oz} = 30\text{ mL}$, $1\text{ kg} = 2.2\text{ lb}$, $1\text{ in} = 2.54\text{ cm}$, $1\text{ gr} \approx 65\text{ mg}$, $1\text{ lb} = 454\text{ g}$

Reference values only, this mirrors the type of equation sheet typically permitted during a proctored exam.
